evals.prompt: In this DSH session, add a scientific-notation calculator. A scoped calculator skill is already available. Please make it usable now.
evals.expected_output: Calls capability_workflow for the concrete calculator need, follows reuse_local by using the scoped calculator capability unchanged, and does not construct, define, or mount a replacement in the parent session.
assertions: Calls capability_workflow before proposing a new plugin.
Does not call cordis_define, cordis_run, cordis_mount, or find_dsh_plugin when local reuse is available.

evals.prompt: Create a live, session-only Cordis Plugin that adds a model-callable tool returning the current UTC time. No matching local capability or acceptable reviewed candidate exists; capability_workflow has returned create_authorized.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the parent Capability Evolution session read-only. Completes the WorkOrder only inside the Host-owned managed child, using the exact Host/Builtin/Tool inspection needed for that tool. Host commits, re-reviews, freezes, and returns a fresh install decision. Claims verified only from a Host tool-roundtrip pass.
assertions: Does not call cordis_define, cordis_run, cordis_mount, or find_dsh_plugin from the parent session.
Constructs only inside the Host-owned managed child after create_authorized.
Does not treat definition or Host activation alone as verified.

evals.prompt: Update @weather_panel so it shows the last refresh time next to the existing status. Keep its Host implementation unchanged unless necessary.
evals.expected_output: Calls capability_workflow with evolve_existing and the named target. The Host-owned managed child edits the known source while the parent stays read-only. Host commits, re-reviews, and returns a fresh install decision. Does not mint a second plugin identity.
assertions: Calls capability_workflow with evolve_existing for the named existing plugin.
Does not call cordis_define or find_dsh_plugin.
Does not create a second Plugin id.

evals.prompt: Create a live dynamic Cordis Plugin that adds a compact refresh button to the current conversation footer. capability_workflow has returned create_authorized. The button should invoke the package's private Host refresh method and show the returned timestamp.
evals.expected_output: After create_authorized, inspects the exact Client Slot contract inside the Host-owned managed child, registers an additive Slot contribution there, and verifies a real Client render and click. The parent session remains read-only and does not call Cordis define/run/mount.
assertions: Inspects the exact target Slot protocol and props before Client registration.
Uses an additive Slot contribution rather than a guessed global DOM selector.
Does not accept Host activation alone as UI verification.
Does not call cordis_define from the parent session.

evals.prompt: Repair @alerts_panel: its latest update fails because the selected event listener has the wrong parameters. If the correction still fails, roll it back to the known current package; do not make a new Plugin.
evals.expected_output: Calls capability_workflow with evolve_existing (repair) and the named target. The Host-owned managed child applies the Event-contract fix; Host commits and re-reviews. If the correction still fails, uses capability_rollback to the known current package. Never skips the workflow or mints a new Plugin id.
assertions: Calls capability_workflow with evolve_existing for the failed package.
Does not call cordis_define(kind:new) or find_dsh_plugin.
Uses capability_rollback for rollback instead of assuming failed update recovery.

evals.prompt: Package my Cordis helper as an npm module, publish it to our registry, and open a release PR with the generated changelog.
evals.expected_output: Does not trigger the AutoEvo capability workflow. Routes the static packaging/release request to the appropriate repository and publication workflow, requiring the relevant user authorization for publication.
assertions: Calls zero Cordis Plugin lifecycle or inspection tools.
Does not claim a dynamic process-local Plugin satisfies a release request.
